decision_rule.CONTRACT_COMPLETE: the documented interface fills the slot; the crate can neither write the slot from safe Rust nor choose its contents from safe Rust; every precondition the crate must rely on is stated by that interface (arity/type, lifetime, reentrancy, ownership transfer, error semantics) for the consumer path that exercises it
decision_rule.CONTRACT_GAP: the edge is real and bounded, but the receipt's basis for it is not the class it is filed under, or a required contract form is missing. The gap and its exact fix (source, receipt or instrument) are named
decision_rule.UNPROVABLE: no instrument or interface establishes the edge at this candidate; what would be needed is named
decision_rule.not_accepted: a class is never accepted on count alone, and a class that rests on an internal closed table is not accepted as a section 7 criterion 2 external ABI contract

obligations.contract: CRYPTO_EX_free's ex_data contract: ptr is NULL or the value stored at this index, a live DynamicDataCtx the enclosing ENGINE owns; release is OwnedCtx::from_raw_at's single block release
obligations.external_caller_class: the crate itself is the installer (the index is created with this hook and stored in a private static) and CRYPTO_free_ex_data is the caller when a dynamic ENGINE dies; a C caller only has to not write a foreign pointer into that index
obligations.can_safe_rust_violate: no. The only writer of the index is dynamic_set_data_ctx (:439, private unsafe fn) through ENGINE_set_ex_data (:713, unsafe pub), and ENGINE_set_ex_data itself is unsafe pub, so no safe path writes the slot. A safe caller cannot even obtain a dynamic ENGINE that owns such a context without unsafe
obligations.evidence_to_establish: the span hash at S (done), the index-provenance chain (:481-488 create, :453 write, :415 release), and a negative control that a foreign write is unreachable from the safe surface (grep of safe pub fns taking raw pointers: 0)

obligations.contract: p is NULL or points at a NUL-terminated C string readable for the call; no ownership taken
obligations.external_caller_class: private unsafe fn, two call kinds: (a) ENGINE_set_default_string (:222, unsafe pub) forwards the C caller's def_list, whose NUL-termination is that caller's obligation; (b) crate error formatters in eng_cnf/evp_cnf/v3_cpols/v3_pci/v3_utl pass crate-owned C strings
obligations.can_safe_rust_violate: no. The fn is private and every caller is unsafe; the C string extent in (a) is the C caller's documented precondition, and in (b) the strings are crate constants or ASN1-owned NUL-terminated buffers
obligations.evidence_to_establish: span hash (done); caller list at S (5 files, all unsafe); the # Safety of ENGINE_set_default_string naming def_list's obligation

obligations.contract: the engine lock is initialised and not held; with a NULL lock the body stops with the list intact (a no-op/leak, not UB); every list member is a live ENGINE
obligations.external_caller_class: registered by the crate itself through engine_cleanup_add_last (:237, pub(crate) unsafe fn) and dispatched from the cleanup stack; the C-side caller is whichever code runs OPENSSL_cleanup (or ENGINE_cleanup, unsafe pub)
obligations.can_safe_rust_violate: not through this callback's arguments (it takes none). The list can only become non-empty through ENGINE_add, which is unsafe pub and takes an Engine* from ENGINE_new/ENGINE_by_id; the head is a private static, so no safe caller can put a foreign pointer in it. A safe caller could run cleanup early (OPENSSL_cleanup), which races only against threads the caller itself started using unsafe APIs - the RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY R1 question
obligations.evidence_to_establish: span hash (done); the private-static writer set (engine_list_add only); the lock-init argument in the # Safety; the TSan schedule result already recorded for RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY
obligations.verdict: SAFETY_DISCHARGED (site-scoped, with the schedule caveat referred to RUNTIME_CONCURRENCY)

obligations.contract: value is NULL or a live CONF_MODULE the calling stack owns and is handing over; module_free releases it and its owned members exactly once
obligations.external_caller_class: OPENSSL_sk_pop_free(to_delete, Some(module_free_thunk)) at :1376, on a local stack built at :1361 from entries popped from the private registry supported_modules (:268)
obligations.can_safe_rust_violate: no. The registry is a private static with private accessors; the only pusher is module_add (:861, unsafe fn) which allocates the ConfModule itself from name/ifunc/ffunc, and the public entry CONF_module_add (:1407) is unsafe. CONF_modules_unload/finish are safe pub but only walk that private stack, so they cannot be made to pass a foreign pointer
obligations.evidence_to_establish: span hash (done); registry provenance (module_add allocates; :929/:1225 are the only pushes; no exported setter takes a ConfModule*)

obligations.contract: data is NULL or the PemPasswordCbData block ui_dup_method_data allocated (this unit's seam); this handle's Drop is its single release; no cleansing needed (function pointer + int, no passphrase)
obligations.external_caller_class: registered as CRYPTO_EX_INDEX_UI_METHOD's free callback by ui_method_data_index_init (:230); CRYPTO_free_ex_data on a UI_METHOD invokes it
obligations.can_safe_rust_violate: no. The value is written by the ex-data new/dup callbacks and the wrapper (:442) using OwnedPwData::zalloc/adopt; writing the slot directly needs CRYPTO_set_ex_data (unsafe pub) on that index, and the index is a private static. Adopter is unsafe fn adopt (:102) with the 'single release' premise
obligations.evidence_to_establish: span hash (done); the creator/adopter chain (zalloc :86, adopt :102, into_raw :112, wrapper :442) and the fact that no safe pub fn reaches this index

mechanism_surface_measured.rule: mechanical: every definition matching 'unsafe extern "C" fn NAME(' in those trees, with the contiguous doc/attribute block above it searched for '# Safety'
mechanism_surface_measured.conclusion: the mechanism's declared surface is no longer unquantified: 0 production definitions in the six declared authority trees lack a written contract. This replaces the prior 'families_total: null' residual with a measured fact. It does NOT establish contract completeness (arity is type-enforced, lifetime/reentrancy/ownership/error are documented only) for the 272 definitions beyond the 5 enrolled

argument: ENGINE_get_first / ENGINE_get_last (src/engine/eng_list.rs:452/:480): read the private list head under the engine lock and return a *mut Engine or NULL. No pointer is dereferenced on the caller's behalf and nothing is released; a safe caller holds an opaque pointer it cannot use without unsafe

CONF_modules_finish / CONF_modules_unload (src/runtime/confmod/mod.rs:1383/:1316): walk crate-private RCU-replaced stacks of crate-allocated modules and release them through module_free_thunk, whose contract is upheld by that provenance (see the fourth obligation above)
OPENSSL_load_builtin_modules (src/runtime/confmod/mod.rs:1526): registers crate-defined static modules; no caller input
safe_surface.conclusion: no safe pub fn in this mechanism takes a raw pointer or a length that reaches an unsafe C-ABI operation with a caller-controlled value (safe_pub_with_raw_pointer_param_reaching_unsafe: 0, re-checked at S). The mechanism's residual is contract completeness, not a safe-interface hole

contract completeness is unadjudicated for 272 of the 277 production definitions; presence of a # Safety is measured, quality is not

the mechanism's unsafe extern "C" fn definitions are installed into externally owned tables (BIO_METHOD, ENGINE, UI_METHOD, ex_data); a C caller that installs them where the contract does not hold is C-invalid, and section 21 rule 1 requires that to be stated rather than assumed - it is stated per site for the 5 enrolled obligations only
C_ABI_CONTRACT.why_not_discharged: the 5 enrolled obligations are each SAFETY_DISCHARGED on a complete per-site argument, and the surface is now measured rather than null; but section 7 criterion 1 applies to every remaining unsafe operation in the mechanism's declared scope, and 272 of the 277 production definitions carry a written contract whose completeness this review did not adjudicate. Presence is not discharge (section 7: 'documentation alone does not discharge an obligation')
